As an addendum to part 1.a., the debate of having volunteer moderators might not be the best choice for VRChat, since having reliable and paid Trust & Safety team holds VRChat as a platform with more integrity. However, if a system were ever to come into place to allow volunteer moderation, an incentive could be for extending the volunteer's VRChat Plus subscription.
Addendum to part 1.b., Zendesk should connect to the in-platform report system so that way, it won't be obscured. When submitting a report ticket, have the platform take our player logs that are requested, so we don't have to go digging in LocalLow for it. Quest users can't even access player logs at all!
Addendum to part 3., for reliable users who volunteer to moderate public lobbies should be given the incentive for free extensions to their VRChat Plus subscriptions.

It isn't the fault of an avatar creator if their NSFW avatar is used in a public space. There are plenty of areas on VRChat where consenting adults can and should be allowed to be NSFW at each other.
And anyway, the way the avatar upload system works, there's no way to know who actually built an avatar - just who uploaded it.
Seems like the report system for groups is much different than the legacy user/world report function.

Hi, I wanted to re-visit this thread and seek it as either Complete/Closed, as most of the concerns listed in my thread have been addressed as best as possible.

I want to thank VRChat's dev team, and the Trust & Safety team for implementing the feedback, and addressing these concerns through that impementation. This thread was written in mid 2022.

Report reasons are now more concise, both in-game and through website tickets. ✅️ (Personally I wish there was still the reason for reporting an Underage user, but there is a more popular Canny post for this)

Groups were new and have been heavily improved with managing, organizing, and moderation. This addresses a user's preference to rather go to a Group instance rather than Public if they want a more moderated experience. ✅️

Age Verification has been implemented. More power for addressing safety. ✅️

Trust & Safety will now send an in-game notification if an in-game report was reviewed and was successful. E-mail responses are more concise. ✅️

Reporting in-game now carries over metadata about the player, and reason for reporting, if the report instead requires a moderation ticket. Excellent win! ✅️

I'm quite satisfied with the moves that have been done since the creation of this post, to improve Safety in VRChat.

details:
Coming back to this after the Avatar Dynamics and OSC update, the "Report Underage Users" thread is now the most popular on the VRChat Canny. I think that it is important that the entire moderation and report system should require an overhaul -- also to include the feature of reporting underage users.
The report system has been in place since pre-Steam release. The "Call Moderator" button was put on the chopping block in mid-2018. The only viable tools that users can perform, are to block, mute, and votekick. Sadly, that doesn't necessarily punish the offending user if they truly are creating a toxic experience for everyone else. Nuisance rank does not seem to be utilized enough.
As for a platform like Rec Room, they have active and unpaid volunteer moderators who can forcibly remove and punish troublemakers in the system. They also utilize 'ToxMod' by Modulate to auto-detect hate-speech, and possibly for detecting very underage users. Afterwards, human moderation review the audio logs to determine the appropriate action.
For example, if you confirm a report on a user from utilizing their in-platform Report system, you won't receive feedback that action had been taken. On top of that, the only way to truly report a malicious user is through the Zendesk ticketing system that VRChat obscures. The VRChat Trust & Safety team is very reliable, but seem to be very limited.
Another problem is that if you report an avatar, it only would only punish the person wearing the avatar, instead of also giving the infraction to the creator of the avatar and taking it down; they get away scott-free. Unoptimized avatars, and sexualized public avatars can become a problem in Quest lobbies where children are present, and I don't want to see the teenage userbase of the platform get exposed to that.
Summary TL;DR:
/1.a. Please overhaul the outdated reporting system. More specificities to reporting users, such as being underage, or utilizing modifications.
/1.b. Make Zendesk tickets more accessible; have them implemented natively in the platform to replace the report system.
/2. There is no two-way communication between the T&S department and user; we don't even have evidence that the native report system works.
/3. Offer reliable VRChat users the chance to voluntarily moderate in public lobbies only, to build a more powerful moderation team. Bring back the Call Moderator button; remove the button for those who abuse the button, or have several infractions.
title: Overhaul the Report system
